title: QUIC RFC 9000 Preferred Address Migration Source Protection
purpose: Describe the bounded runtime proof for the remaining RFC 9000 Section 9.6.3 preferred-address migration-source and client-address validation tail.
design_summary: The preferred-address tail reuses the current single-active-path migration runtime. A path that matches the peer preferred_address transport parameter remains a candidate path until validation succeeds. When the client-side path changes, same-family IPv4 or IPv6 preferred-address candidates are validated and promoted only after path-validation success. Preferred-address traffic from a changed source is protected by the same candidate validation and anti-amplification accounting used for migration candidates, and probe packets from a different address trigger a PATH_CHALLENGE without promoting the path first.
data_and_state_considerations: The proof relies on committed peer transport parameters, candidate-path validation state, anti-amplification counters, and active-path promotion effects. The runtime keeps preferred-address matching as address-and-port comparison against the parsed IPv4 and IPv6 preferred_address values and does not add a public migration API in this slice.
edge_cases_and_constraints: IPv4 and IPv6 preferred-address candidates are exercised as distinct same-family migration choices.
A preferred-address packet from a changed source remains amplification-limited until validation succeeds.
Probe-triggered PATH_CHALLENGE emission does not imply active-path promotion before validation.
The proof keeps the existing single-active-path model and does not claim multipath scheduling.
alternatives_considered: Leave the requirements under the broad RFC 9000 umbrella artifacts; rejected because generated triage needed direct focused proof for the remaining S9P6P3 tail.
Broaden the slice into all remaining migration-core requirements; rejected because the unblocked preferred-address tail is smaller and adjacent to the already-landed S9P6P2 cutover work.
Add a new runtime preferred-address selector API; rejected because the current trace gap is direct proof over existing candidate-path behavior, not a public API request.
risks: The slice proves runtime transition behavior, not hosted endpoint interop across real network interfaces.
The implementation remains single-active-path and does not claim concurrent multipath use.
The proof treats parser/opened-datagram path identities as the observable seam for client and server preferred-address behavior.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This design covers S9P6P3-0006, S9P6P3-0009, and S9P6P3-0010 only: same-family preferred-address selection proof, changed-source protection, and probe-triggered client-address validation.
